topIssues.title: op-node: CriticalErrorEvent for deposits-only attributes failure causes permanent node crash loop
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
## Description

`DepositsOnlyPayloadAttributesRequestEvent` error handling emits `CriticalErrorEvent`, which kills the node permanently. Under certain conditions — particularly involving the SuperAuthority deny path — this error is hit due to a transient state mismatch, not a true critical failure. Because the deny list is persistent, every restart hits the same crash, creating an infinite crash loop.

## Root Cause

`DepositsOnlyAttributes()` has sanity checks that assume `lastAttribs` is always populated when called. This held for the original Holocene invalid-payload flow, where `DepositsOnlyPayloadAttributesRequestEvent` is only emitted immediately after `NextAttributes` sets `lastAttribs`.

However, `DepositsOnlyPayloadAttributesRequestEvent` can also be emitted from `PayloadProcessEvent` via the SuperAuthority deny path (`payload_process.go`). In this path, a `ResetEvent` can be processed between the `BuildStartEvent` that initiated the payload and the `PayloadProcessEvent` that checks the deny list — because events are queued, not inline. When that happens, the pipeline reset clears `lastAttribs` to nil, and `DepositsOnlyAttributes()` fails with `"no attributes generated yet"`.

## Event Ordering Leading to Crash

1. `ForkchoiceUpdateEvent` → triggers `ResetEvent` (queued)
2. `ResetEvent` → pipeline reset, **`lastAttribs = nil`**
3. `BuildStartedEvent` → `BuildSealEvent` → `PayloadProcessEvent`
4. Deny check fires → `DepositsOnlyPayloadAttributesRequestEvent`
5. `DepositsOnlyAttributes()` → `lastAttribs == nil` → **crash** (`CriticalErrorEvent`)

## Impact

- The node crashes permanently with `"deriving deposits-only attributes: no attributes generated yet"`
- Since the deny list persists across restarts, every new node instance re-derives the same denied block and hits the same crash
- This creates an unrecoverable crash loop requiring manual intervention

## Supernode Context

This is particularly problematic in the supernode, where chain containers manage virtual nodes (VNs). After multiple reorg cycles, the chain accumulates deposits-only blocks from prior cycles. When a new VN re-derives and encounters one of these prior deposits-only blocks, the event ordering race described above can occur, permanently crashing the VN.

## Expected Behavior

The error should be treated as a transient state mismatch (like other similar cases in the derivation pipeline) and trigger a `ResetEvent` instead of `CriticalErrorEvent`. On reset, the pipeline re-derives from L1, re-populates `lastAttribs` via `NextAttributes`, and the deny check succeeds on retry.

## References

- Fix PR: ethereum-optimism/optimism#19417
- Discovered via supernode interop reorg/eviction tests: ethereum-optimism/optimism#19346

topIssues.title: kona/derive: system config update errors in StatefulAttributesBuilder return Critical instead of being ignored
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
## Problem

In [`stateful.rs:114-120`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/48b31f0b1b1e9afcf4d07f75c28771f602cc6a1b/rust/kona/crates/protocol/derive/src/attributes/stateful.rs#L114-L120), errors from `update_with_receipts` are mapped to `Critical`:

```rust
sys_config
    .update_with_receipts(
        &receipts,
        self.rollup_cfg.l1_system_config_address,
        self.rollup_cfg.is_ecotone_active(header.timestamp),
    )
    .map_err(|e| PipelineError::SystemConfigUpdate(e).crit())?; // ← wrong
```

[`update_with_receipts`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/48b31f0b1b1e9afcf4d07f75c28771f602cc6a1b/rust/kona/crates/protocol/genesis/src/system/config.rs#L122-L148) uses `try_for_each` with `?`, meaning the **first malformed `ConfigUpdate` log** aborts the scan and returns an error. That error then halts derivation via `Critical`.

All `SystemConfigUpdateError` variants are triggered by **bad external L1 data**: invalid log structure, unknown update type, bad ABI encoding, etc.

## Why it matters

Any L1 transaction that emits a malformed `ConfigUpdate` event at the `SystemConfig` contract address would permanently halt kona derivation.

## Correct behaviour

The Go op-node intentionally **ignores** all system config update errors in the attributes builder:

```go
// errors from UpdateSystemConfigWithL1Receipts are ignored as they represent malformed or invalid updates
// and there is no recovery mechanism for malformed updates, we must process past them.
_ = UpdateSystemConfigWithL1Receipts(&sysConfig, receipts, ba.rollupCfg, info.Time())
```

Note: the traversal stage in kona **already handles this correctly** — it logs a warning and continues on `update_with_receipts` errors. Only the attributes builder has the wrong behaviour.

## Fix

```rust
if let Err(e) = sys_config.update_with_receipts(
    &receipts,
    self.rollup_cfg.l1_system_config_address,
    self.rollup_cfg.is_ecotone_active(header.timestamp),
) {
    warn!(target: "attributes_builder", ?e, "Failed to update system config from L1 receipts, ignoring");
}
```

## Parent issue

Part of #19510

topPRs.title: interop: add strong consistency guarantees
topPRs.author: karlfloersch
topPRs.body:
Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19420

## Summary

This PR refactors the supernode interop activity around a single persisted transition model so that normal execution and crash recovery use the same apply path.

For a new reader, the important mental model is:

1. `progressAndRecord()` is the top-level interop tick.
2. If a `PendingTransition` already exists in `VerifiedDB`, interop replays it.
3. Otherwise interop observes the world, verifies the next timestamp, builds a `PendingTransition`, persists it, and applies it immediately.
4. The transition stays in the WAL until all of its side effects succeed.

This is the minimal-diff version of the stronger consistency work: it keeps the existing package structure, but makes the state transitions explicit and replayable.

Context: this work is informed by the Runtime Verification audit writeup here:
- https://github.com/runtimeverification/_audits_Ethereum-optimism_optimism_interopv2/issues/8

## What Changed

### 1. Unified normal execution and recovery

Interop no longer has separate "normal apply" and "startup recovery" logic for the important state transitions.

Instead, effectful decisions are represented as a generic `PendingTransition` stored in `VerifiedDB`, and both steady-state execution and restart recovery go through the same `applyPendingTransition()` path.

This covers:
- `DecisionAdvance`
- `DecisionInvalidate`
- `DecisionRewind`

### 2. Verification is now read-only

`verify()` no longer mutates `logsDB` while deciding whether a frontier is valid.

Instead:
- frontier verification uses an in-memory `frontierView`
- accepted-history lookups still come from `logsDB`
- frontier logs are only persisted later, during `DecisionAdvance` transition apply

That makes the WAL the real boundary for stateful changes.

### 3. Advance / invalidate / rewind are explicit transition kinds

`buildPendingTransition()` now constructs explicit transition payloads.

Notably:
- rewind uses an explicit `RewindPlan`
- advance persists exact frontier blocks during apply
- invalidation preserves the WAL until all invalidation side effects succeed

### 4. Replays are idempotent where they need to be

To support "persist first, clear last":
- `VerifiedDB.Commit()` is idempotent for exact duplicate replays
- rewind apply reports all failures, but keeps the WAL until the transition converges
- invalidation and rewind failures preserve the transition for retry
- invalid rewind WAL state now fails closed instead of being silently cleared

### 5. Top-level interop flow is easier to read again

The orchestration is back to a simpler shape:
- `progressAndRecord()` owns the transition lifecycle
- `progressInterop()` computes the next action
- `checkPreconditions()` gates verification
- `decideVerifiedResult()` interprets verification output

Dead wrappers and stale helper paths were removed along the way.

### 6. Reset callbacks are no longer part of interop correctness

Interop now treats `Reset()` as a no-op interface shim. The actual correctness path is the persisted transition apply logic.

The broader chain-container rewind/invalidation APIs are still powerful footguns, so this PR adds explicit comments/TODOs documenting that they should only be used from interop transition application until that interface is narrowed further.

### 7. Small cleanup and reviewability improvements

Also included in this branch:
- removed dead denylist clearing APIs (`ClearDenied`, `DenyList.Clear`)
- removed dead helpers/wrappers (`loadLogs`, `rewindAccepted`, `RewindAfter`, etc.)
- clarified the logsDB warning for chains with block times greater than one second
- cleaned up stale comments and compatibility artifacts

## Current Top-Level Flow

```text
Start
  -> progressAndRecord
     -> if pending transition exists:
          applyPendingTransition
     -> else:
          progressInterop
            -> observeRound
            -> checkPreconditions
            -> verify
            -> decideVerifiedResult
          -> if wait (DecisionWait):
               refreshCurrentL1OnWait
          -> if rewind with no prior verified state:
               return early (nothing to rewind)
          -> else (advance, invalidate, or rewind):
               buildPendingTransition
               SetPendingTransition
               applyPendingTransition
```

## Follow-Up

A follow-up PR should remove the ability to trigger rewinds/reorg side effects from outside interop until cross-activity concurrency between these stateful operations is fully designed and enforced.

Today the code documents those APIs as dangerous footguns, but the safer end state is to narrow that surface so interop transition application is the only place allowed to drive rewinds.

## Why This Is Better

Compared with `develop`, this branch moves the interop activity closer to an explicit transaction model:
- decisions are separated from side effects
- recovery and steady-state share the same apply path
- frontier verification no longer mutates durable state
- WAL clearing happens only after the transition has been applied

That makes the database/control-flow behavior much easier to review in one place.

Just as importantly, the consistency checks (L1 fork verification, accepted snapshot re-verification, stale logsDB detection) ensure that each virtual node's local data is internally consistent before interop cross-validates across chains. This means cross-validation only ever operates on trustworthy inputs.

## Files To Read First

If you are new to this diff, start here:
- `op-supernode/supernode/activity/interop/interop.go`
- `op-supernode/supernode/activity/interop/verified_db.go`
- `op-supernode/supernode/activity/interop/logdb.go`
- `op-supernode/supernode/activity/interop/verification_view.go`
- `op-supernode/supernode/chain_container/invalidation.go`

## Test Plan

Rerun coverage I checked while updating this branch:
- [x] `go test ./op-supernode/supernode/activity/interop/... -count=1`
- [x] `go test ./op-supernode/supernode/activity/superroot -count=1`

Focused regressions added/updated on this branch include:
- pending advance replay after commit succeeds idempotently
- pending invalidate/rewind transitions are preserved on failure
- rewind apply reports all failures
- invalid rewind WAL state fails closed
- frontier verification does not persist frontier logs

topPRs.title: chore(op-e2e): migrate Makefile to justfile
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
## Summary
- Migrates op-e2e build targets from Make to Just, following the same pattern used by other packages (op-node, op-batcher, etc.)
- Replaces the 73-line Makefile with a justfile that preserves all targets: test, test-ws, test-actions, test-http, test-cannon, test-fault-proofs, fuzz, clean, gen-binding, cannon-prestates, and test-external (now parameterized)
- The Makefile becomes a deprecated shim that delegates to just with a deprecation warning, preserving backwards compatibility

## Key changes
- `JUNIT_FILE` conditional logic uses just's `env()` and `if` expressions
- `test-external-%` Make pattern becomes `test-external NAME` with a parameter
- `pre-test-cannon` directory check uses a shebang script
- `gen-binding` requires `CONTRACT` as a just parameter instead of Make variable
- `num_cores` uses just's built-in `num_cpus()`
- `clean` uses `rm -rf` (safe flag) instead of `rm -r`

## Test plan
